evidence_grounded_scientific_claim: Interfacial-potential or electric-field changes co-occur with changes in carrier decay or extraction kinetics.
how_the_measurements_are_complementary: The pair connects an energetic/electrostatic change to its carrier-kinetic response in the same treatment comparison.
relevance_to_the_present_experiment: Relative dark/light surface-potential signals and relative ΔSP were measured. TRPL/carrier lifetime was not measured and is retained only as broader carrier-dynamics context.
interpretation_limit: Lifetime direction is context dependent: shorter decay can indicate faster extraction or stronger recombination. Co-observation is not causation.

evidence_grounded_scientific_claim: Interfacial-potential changes co-occur with changes in radiative emission yield or net non-radiative loss.
how_the_measurements_are_complementary: The pair tests whether energetic-interface modification is accompanied by a change in emissive quality.
relevance_to_the_present_experiment: Closest present-study analogue: relative dark/light surface-potential signals or relative ΔSP paired with steady-state PL peak intensity. PLQY was not measured.
interpretation_limit: PL intensity also depends on excitation, absorption, thickness, collection, and stack geometry. Co-observation is not causation.

evidence_grounded_scientific_claim: Changes in the spatial surface-potential landscape co-occur with changes in carrier decay or extraction kinetics.
how_the_measurements_are_complementary: The pair links where electrostatic heterogeneity occurs to how long carriers persist or how rapidly they transfer.
relevance_to_the_present_experiment: Relative dark/light surface-potential signals and relative ΔSP were measured. TRPL/carrier lifetime was not measured and is retained only as broader carrier-dynamics context.
interpretation_limit: Spatial scales and sampled regions may differ, and lifetime direction remains mechanism dependent. Co-observation is not causation.

evidence_grounded_scientific_claim: Surface-potential magnitude or uniformity changes co-occur with changes in emission intensity, yield, or homogeneity.
how_the_measurements_are_complementary: The pair distinguishes electrostatic uniformity from emissive uniformity and tests whether both respond to the same treatment.
relevance_to_the_present_experiment: Closest present-study analogue: relative dark/light surface-potential signals or relative ΔSP paired with steady-state PL peak intensity. PLQY was not measured.
interpretation_limit: Matched fields of view are needed for a spatial claim; ensemble co-trends alone are not causal evidence.

evidence_grounded_scientific_claim: Work-function or energy-level-alignment changes co-occur with changes in carrier-transfer or recombination kinetics.
how_the_measurements_are_complementary: The pair connects an energy-level-alignment measurement to a kinetic response relevant to charge transfer.
relevance_to_the_present_experiment: Broader context only: neither calibrated work function nor TRPL/carrier lifetime was measured. The present KPFM output is an uncalibrated relative surface-potential signal, not work function.
interpretation_limit: Absolute work function requires calibrated tip/sign conventions, and lifetime direction is architecture dependent.

evidence_grounded_scientific_claim: Work-function or energy-level-alignment changes co-occur with changes in radiative emission efficiency.
how_the_measurements_are_complementary: The pair tests whether energy-level tuning is accompanied by a measurable emissive response.
relevance_to_the_present_experiment: Steady-state PL peak intensity was measured, but PLQY and calibrated work function were not. The present uncalibrated relative surface-potential signal is not equivalent to work function.
interpretation_limit: Only one retained relationship supports this pairing, and the current experiment uses surface potential rather than calibrated work function.
